findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the once-per-process enforcement mechanism: either use `via='warning'` (Python's warnings module deduplicates by call site per process) OR add a module-level `_rebar_llm_model_warned: set[str]` guard in `model_classes.py` before calling `warn_deprecated`, and state the choice explicitly so the implementer doesn't have to guess.

findings.finding: The plan mandates 'emits a deprecation warning ONCE per process' but does not specify the implementation mechanism that achieves it. warn_deprecated has no built-in deduplication: with via='log' (the default channel used by all existing callers) logging fires on every call; with via='warning' Python's warnings module deduplicates by (message, category, module, lineno) per process and achieves once-per-process automatically. Because load_class_slots() is called at every slot-resolution point, a via='log' implementation would emit the warning on every LLM operation that touches the class system — contradicting the stated behavior and the AC.
findings.location: Approach section ('emits a deprecation warning ONCE per process') and AC line 2 ('the deprecation warning is emitted once, not per call')
scenarios: An operator runs a gate review: load_class_slots() is called N times across N LLM operations; with via='log' the deprecation warning fires N times per process, violating the stated guarantee

An implementer chooses via='log' (the default) and writes the 'once per call' AC test against a subprocess, passes the subprocess test, but ships an implementation that emits on every call in production
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope / model_classes.py bullet, add: 'Emit via via="warning" so Python's warnings module provides once-per-process deduplication at the call site — no separate flag required. Alternatively, guard with a module-level set `_WARNED: set[str] = set()` and skip the warn_deprecated call if the key is already in it.' Pick one and state it.

findings.finding: The deprecation warning's 'once per process' flag is module-level mutable state, but the plan is silent on thread safety. If `_deprecations.warn_deprecated` uses a custom module-level seen-set or bool (rather than delegating entirely to the Python `warnings` module's C-level deduplication), two threads entering the warning path simultaneously can both observe the flag as unset, execute a check-then-act race, and both emit the warning — violating the 'exactly once' contract the AC tests rely on.
findings.location: Scope — `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` / AC: 'the deprecation warning is emitted once, not per call'
scenarios: Remote MCP server shape: the MCP server handles concurrent client requests in a thread pool; two simultaneous requests both carrying `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` in their environment context could race through the once-check and both emit the warning, potentially surprising operators monitoring for a single deprecation signal and undermining the 'once' guarantee the AC asserts.
findings.suggested_fix: If `warn_deprecated` delegates to `warnings.warn(…, stacklevel=N)` with the default `'once'` or `'default'` filter, the CPython `warnings` C module's seen-set IS GIL-protected and no extra locking is needed — state that explicitly. If it uses a Python-level `set` or `bool`, wrap the check-and-set in a `threading.Lock` initialised at module import.

If the built-in filter already handles deduplication, the custom flag and the mandated subprocess test may be over-engineering relative to prior art; if `warn_deprecated` uses a custom flag, the plan should note why the built-in filter was rejected.

findings.finding: The plan places the 'maps to ALL THREE classes' fan-out in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, but class slots are resolved by `model_classes.load_class_slots()` / `parse_class_slots()` in `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — a separate module with a strictly one-way dependency (model_classes imports config; config must never import model_classes at module scope, per an existing lazy-import invariant). The plan gives no mechanism for how `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set in `config.py`'s `from_env()` will populate all three class slots resolved later in `model_classes.py`. The implementer must choose between mutually incompatible strategies (synthesize `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` env side-effects at `from_env` time; intercept in `load_class_slots` to check the deprecated var as a fallback; thread a new parameter from `LLMConfig` into the class resolver) — none of which is described, and each has different blast radius and testability.
findings.location: Scope: src/rebar/llm/config.py — 'the map-to-all-three behaviour'

findings.finding: The plan's core behavioral protocol — 'REBAR_LLM_MODEL maps to ALL THREE classes' — is stated as a requirement but the interception mechanism is never specified. The existing code resolves REBAR_LLM_MODEL into cfg.model (a single scalar, config.py:469), while class slot resolution happens separately in model_classes.py via parse_class_slots/load_class_slots. The plan does not say whether the mapping works by (a) setting all three REBAR_LLM_{CLASS}_MODEL env vars before class-slot resolution, (b) intercepting in resolve_model_string to treat cfg.model as the class-slot default, (c) populating ClassSlot defaults at parse_class_slots call time, or (d) some other approach. Without a specified interception point, the AC ('all three classes resolve to that model') is ambiguous for an implementer.
findings.location: Approach section ('maps to ALL THREE classes') and Scope ('src/rebar/llm/config.py — the map-to-all-three behaviour')
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope entry for config.py, add: 'When REBAR_LLM_MODEL is set and no per-class REBAR_LLM_{CLASS}_MODEL env var is set for a given class, the fallback default inside _parse_slot (model_classes.py:148) is replaced by the REBAR_LLM_MODEL value, so all three slots inherit it.' Alternatively, specify that config.py inserts synthetic REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL/STANDARD_MODEL/TRIVIAL_MODEL env reads that fall back to REBAR_LLM_MODEL.

findings.finding: The plan states that when REBAR_LLM_MODEL is set and no per-class configuration exists, 'all three classes resolve to that model' — but the plan does not specify WHERE in the resolution chain this injection occurs. The existing parse_class_slots() in model_classes.py reads per-class env vars (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL) independently and falls back to DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS built-in defaults; it knows nothing about REBAR_LLM_MODEL. The Scope names only config.py as the implementation site. It is unresolved whether the shim sets the per-class env vars at import time, overrides the defaults passed into _parse_slot, or wraps parse_class_slots() at a higher level — each choice has different precedence semantics.
